title: Money, banking & central banks
examples: What is the main job of a central bank?
How do regular banks make money?
Does lending money actually increase the total money in the economy?

explain.say: Today we learn about money and banks. First we look at what money actually does for us.

items: Money acts as a medium of exchange

draw.text: Functions of Money: Medium of Exchange

explain.say: Money also acts as a unit of account. This means it helps us measure value easily.
The third function is a store of value. You can keep money to use later.

items: Money can be held for future use

explain.say: Now we look at credit creation. Banks lend money and this increases the total money supply.
For example, if you deposit one hundred pounds in a bank, they might lend out ninety pounds. This is credit creation.
In real life, when a shop buys goods using a bank loan, that loan creates new money in the economy.

draw.text: Real Life: Shop Buys Goods with Loan

faq.q: What is the difference between the central bank and regular banks?
faq.a: The central bank controls the money supply for the whole country. Regular banks take deposits and give out loans to people and businesses.
asks: What is the role of the central bank?

faq.q: If banks create money, does this mean the government prints it?
faq.a: No, the central bank controls the printing of physical money. Banks create money through lending, which is a separate process.
asks: Does the central bank print all the money?
Is money creation the same as printing money?

faq.q: What is the reserve requirement for banks?
faq.a: The reserve requirement is the fraction of deposits banks must keep in reserve. This controls how much money they can lend out.
asks: How much money must banks hold?
What limits how much banks can lend?

faq.q: Can credit creation only happen if people borrow money?
faq.a: Credit creation happens when banks issue loans. The borrower then spends that money, increasing the money supply.
asks: What triggers the creation of new money?

faq.a: No, money includes digital forms like bank transfers. These electronic transactions are part of the money supply.

facts: Money serves three main functions: medium of exchange, unit of account, and store of value.
Credit creation occurs when banks issue loans using deposited funds.
The central bank oversees the banking system to maintain stability.
The reserve requirement dictates the portion of deposits banks must keep.

quiz.say: Which function allows us to compare the price of apples to the price of books?
quiz.why: The unit of account provides a common standard for measuring value.

wrong.0: This is about controlling the banking system, not measuring value.
wrong.2: This is for trading goods directly, not measuring value.
wrong.3: This relates to keeping money for later use.

quiz.say: If a bank lends out ninety pounds from a one hundred pound deposit, what is the immediate effect?
quiz.why: Lending money to someone else increases the total money circulating in the economy.

wrong.1: The deposit amount itself does not change just because a loan is made.
wrong.2: The reserve requirement is a rule, not something that changes with one loan.
wrong.3: The central bank only steps in if the system is unstable.

quiz.say: What is the primary role of the central bank in relation to banks?

options.show: To maintain the stability of the banking system
options.say: To maintain the stability of the banking system

options.show: To print all the physical cash
options.say: To print all the physical cash

options.show: To decide interest rates for consumers
options.say: To decide interest rates for consumers

quiz.why: The central bank acts as the bank for other banks, keeping the system stable.

wrong.0: Their focus is on domestic financial stability, not global trade management.
wrong.2: While they control printing, their role is broader than just printing.
wrong.3: They influence rates, but commercial banks set the final consumer rates.
